solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bite head off tiger in shocker (6)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a Taser is a stun gun, a shocker
the head of tiger, placed inside TASER after TAS

explanation.surface: A zookeeper is warned that a biting tiger may need a stun gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads as decapitation, but it only takes the first letter of tiger to slip inside the shocker.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small sample of food, a bite to try it.

clue.text: What will activate journalist who’s a bad speller? (4,6)

blocks.note: a device that switches something on at a preset hour
split 5,5 it is a writer for a London paper who casts spells, a bad speller in the magic sense

explanation.surface: A newspaper reader grumbles about a reporter who cannot spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is a London newspaper. A speller here is not someone who spells words but someone who casts spells, and a bad one is a witch.
explanation.definitionFit: A time switch is the clock-driven device that activates heating or lights.

clue.text: Pressure breaking sharpish utensil (5)

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: sharpish = soon, promptly
P is the symbol for pressure, placed inside SOON

explanation.surface: A cheap knife snaps under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharpish' looks like a description of the utensil, but it means soon, as in 'get here sharpish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain category definition: the answer is one of the everyday kitchen utensils.

clue.text: Earnest strains from One Direction? (7)

indicators.note: to strain something is to twist and stretch it out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A serious-sounding song by the boy band One Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is a boy band, so 'strains' look like tunes; the definition is simply one of the compass directions, east.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern means coming from one direction, the east.

clue.text: Case of effectiveness by a cool hero (8)

indicators.note: a word's case is its outside, so take its first and last letters

blocks.note: used as itself
chill = cool
the outer letters of effectiveness

explanation.surface: An argument that a calm hero gets results.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is written with the case last, though the clue gives it first: 'by' lets it stand beside A CHILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the Greek hero of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Native American leader of different faith (5)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the Cree are a Native American people
the first letter of different

explanation.surface: A Native American chief follows another religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native American leader' reads as one chief; split it after American.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of religious beliefs, a faith.

clue.text: Paint gone in one second (7)

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
a mo is a moment, a second
past = gone, placed inside MO

explanation.surface: Paint dries in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paint' is the definition, not a verb; MO is British informal for a moment, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint laid on thickly so the brush strokes stand out.

clue.text: Subsequently, are United outside the box? (9)

blocks.note: later = subsequently
to ally is to unite, so 'they ally' = 'they are united'

explanation.surface: A football fan wonders whether Manchester United will later sit out of the penalty box.
explanation.walkthrough: United looks like a football club, but here 'are united' is a verb phrase that becomes ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom match: thinking outside the box and thinking sideways both mean approaching a problem unconventionally.

clue.text: Staple of vegan diet, say, cooked with a bit of oil (4)

indicators.note: cooked food has been worked over, so the letters are rearranged
a bit of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: used as itself
the first letter of oil

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: fry the vegan staple with a drop of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya beans and their products are a staple protein in a vegan diet.

clue.text: Had an angle perhaps about popular ancient history? (8)

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: 'that's ancient history' = 'that's finished'

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: to angle is to fish, so 'had an angle' = fished
in = popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether a trendy history book was written with a slant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had an angle' suggests bias; the angler's sense gives FISHED. The definition is a phrase: something that is ancient history is over and done with.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something ancient history means it is finished and no longer matters.

clue.text: Garbage by night light? (9)

blocks.note: nonsense, foolish talk
the glow of the moon, taken literally

explanation.surface: Rubbish put out beside a night light.
explanation.walkthrough: Garbage suggests bins; it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine means foolish talk, garbage, and also moonlight.

clue.text: Waste collector out to lunch (5)

blocks.note: a small pot a toddler uses as a toilet
British informal for crazy

explanation.surface: The binman is off on his lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: Potty (crazy) is British informal; out to lunch is slang for not all there.
explanation.definitionFit: A potty collects a toddler's waste, and potty also means mad.

clue.text: A concern at the end of the day? (6,8)

definitions.text: A concern at the end of the day?

blocks.note: reads as a worry, but a concern is also a business

blocks.clueFragment: at the end of the day?
blocks.note: a stock phrase for 'ultimately', here taken literally as dusk: a business in its last hours

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is worrying them as the day closes.
explanation.walkthrough: Concern means a business, not a worry, and 'at the end of the day' is a stock phrase that here means literally at sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunset industry is one in decline, a business near the end of its day.

clue.text: Asian in river and swimming in sea (10)

indicators.note: letters swimming move about freely, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: used as itself
the Don is a river in Russia and several in Britain
the letters of IN SEA rearranged

explanation.surface: An Asian traveller takes a dip in a river and then in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is used as itself, while the second is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indonesian is a person from Indonesia, in Asia.

clue.text: Problematically, where worms found from Cuzco? (5)

blocks.note: the IN of 'in a can of worms', a problematic state
a can of worms is where worms are found

explanation.surface: A gardener in Peru wonders where the worms have got to.
explanation.walkthrough: Being in a can of worms means being in a mess, so 'problematically' supplies the IN. Cuzco was the capital of the Inca empire, in Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Incan describes anything of the Incas, whose capital was Cuzco.

clue.text: Storing charge, battery unit before a storm (9)

blocks.note: a battery is made of cells
used as itself
to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: A battery is charged in anticipation of a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storing charge' reads as electrical, matching the battery; it is a fee for storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellarage is the fee charged for storing goods in a cellar.

clue.text: Mean spirit wildly booing, with exhausted bull held by horns at first (9)

indicators.note: wildly signals disorder, so the letters are rearranged
exhausted means emptied out, so only the outer letters remain
held by the horns: the jumble is gripped by the H at its front
at first takes the first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of horns
letters for the anagram
bull emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: A crowd jeers at a spent bull grabbed by the horns in a bullring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like average; a mean spirit is a malicious one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobgoblin is a mischievous, ill-natured sprite.

clue.text: Bill in tangle, undoing nets (8)

indicators.note: to net something is to catch it, so one word traps the other

blocks.note: bane = ruin, one's undoing
a knot is a tangle, caught inside BANE

explanation.surface: A beak is caught up in a tangle of netting as someone frees it.
explanation.walkthrough: Undoing looks like an anagram signal and nets like fodder, but undoing is the outer word BANE and nets the instruction to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bill is the usual American word for a paper note of money.

clue.text: American players’ association in Panama City (9)

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: Colón is a city in Panama
RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, the London drama school, placed inside COLON

explanation.surface: A union of American athletes is based in Panama City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama City' looks like the capital, but it means a city in Panama: Colón.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a native of Colorado is one kind of American.

clue.text: Chestnut tree? (7)

blocks.note: reads as a species of tree, but as a colour it is reddish brown
the question mark flags that the tree is named for the colour of its timber

explanation.walkthrough: Chestnut names a colour, reddish brown, not the species of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A redwood is a tree with reddish, chestnut-coloured wood.

clue.text: Authority keeps mum? (3-2)

blocks.note: keeping mum is saying nothing; this supplies the saying
mum = silent, nothing, the letter O as zero

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a boss keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: O looks like zero, so 'says nothing' becomes SAYS O.
explanation.definitionFit: Say-so means authority, as in 'on whose say-so?'.

clue.text: One’s tight corset initially goes in or goes out (7)

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter
the C goes in with the other letters
going out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of corset
used as itself
used as itself

explanation.surface: A tight corset may be put on or taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like a snug corset; it means stingy. Scrooge is the miser in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scrooge is a miser, one who is tight with money.

clue.text: Official house for native of the tropics? (8,6)

blocks.note: a mandarin is a senior official
the House of Orange is the Dutch royal house

explanation.surface: A civil servant is posted to a residence in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' reads as a person; here it is a fruit that grows in warm climates.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarin orange is a citrus fruit native to warm, tropical and subtropical Asia.

clue.text: Penny under are you in foreign cash? (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so it follows

blocks.note: text-speak spelling of 'are you'
P is short for penny, and 'p' is said 'pee'

explanation.surface: A tourist asks whether a coin is in the local currency.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain prices in pence are spoken as 'ten pee', so penny = PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India and other countries.

clue.text: Angel in heaven, you suffer less heartache, ultimately (5)

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take last letters

blocks.clueFragment: in heaven, you suffer less heartache
blocks.note: the last letters of heaven, you, suffer, less, heartache

explanation.surface: A comforting promise that in heaven there will be less pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the link; the last letters start at heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurses are often called angels for their care.

clue.text: Topping gone, burning cakes while in oven (4)

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, and it goes
to cake is to coat all over, so one word encases the other

blocks.note: HOT = burning, with its first letter removed
as = while, placed inside OT

explanation.surface: Cakes left in the oven start to burn.
explanation.walkthrough: Cakes looks like baking in the oven; here it is a verb meaning encases.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops.

clue.text: Fashionable needs of French mission (5)

indicators.note: something that needs a thing lacks it, so it is taken away

blocks.note: à la mode = fashionable
DE is French for 'of', removed from the end

explanation.surface: A stylish look is required for a French diplomatic posting.
explanation.walkthrough: Mission suggests a diplomatic task; it is a Spanish mission building in Texas, famous for its siege in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was a Spanish mission in San Antonio, Texas.

clue.text: Stew pan ending on floor, serve one sandwiches (9)

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter
to sandwich something is to put it between, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a pot is a pan
to pour is to serve a drink
I = one
the last letter of floor, sandwiched in POURI

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: a pan of stew ends up on the floor while someone serves.
explanation.walkthrough: Potpourri is best known as dried petals, but its original sense is a stew or mixed dish of meats.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot-pourri, literally 'rotten pot' in French, first meant a stew of mixed meats.

clue.text: More in ground interred! (8)

indicators.note: ground up means broken down, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone buried in the ground exclaims about more of them underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In ground' reads as a burial, but 'in' belongs with 'More' as the definition, and ground is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable, so more in means trendier.

clue.text: Separate northern river (6)

blocks.note: to sever is to separate
N = northern

explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and western England.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is Britain's longest river, flowing from Wales through western England.
